newsitem.title: CANADA: CANADA'S PRAIRIES TO SEE COOLER TEMPS, LITTLE RAIN.
newsitem.headline: CANADA'S PRAIRIES TO SEE COOLER TEMPS, LITTLE RAIN.

text.p: Canada's Prairies on Monday were forecast to see cooler temperatures but little rain to Thursday, an Environment Canada meteorologist said.

A low pressure ridge over central Saskatchewan Monday was forecast to be followed by a cold front with rain of up to 20 to 30 mm (1.2 inch) mainly over the bush country north of the Prairie grainbelt, meteorologist Francois Choquet said.
Highs to Thursday were forecast to be in the low 20s Celsius (68 F) with overnight lows of five Celsius (40 F).
A southerly air flow on Thursday was expected to bring warmer temperatures to Saskatchewan and Manitoba, he said.
The northern half of Alberta and Saskatchewan were forecast to see up to five mm (0.2 inch) of rain, he added.
